keyframe_review.note: New keyframe (Cliopatria has no Rapa Nui row). Infobox area 163.6 km2 (no date); at the grid's resolution the island is one cell (about 253 km2). One island, one chiefdom from settlement; the island was divided between two confederations (hanau) 'by the 15th century' and the 'Otu 'Itu fought the Tu'u 'from 1724 until 1750' and 'until the 1860s' (Easter Island page) without a recorded split of the territory.

region.text: Easter Island (Rapa Nui), 163.6 km2 (Easter Island infobox)

ledger.note: 1200: the Polynesian chiefdom of Rapa Nui begins with the settlement of the island. The page gives a range, not a year: arrival 'around the year 800', 'closer to 1200' (2007 study), estimates 'from 400 to 1300 CE' with the current best in the 12th century, and the island 'was colonized late, about 1200 CE'; the date of Hotu Matuʻa's arrival is not given. 1200 is the latest of the page's figures, used as a bridging start.

region.text: Easter Island (Rapa Nui), 163.6 km2 (Easter Island infobox)

ledger.note: 1888: the chiefs cede Rapa Nui's sovereignty to Chile. 'On September 9, 1888' the Agreement of Wills (Acuerdo de Voluntades) was signed and Atamu Tekena 'ceded the sovereignty of the island to the State of Chile', represented by Policarpo Toro (the History of Easter Island page adds that the Rapa Nui 'sold nothing').

wars.name: Peruvian slave raids
wars.outcome: 'More than 1400 Rapanui islanders were kidnapped, about half of the island's population'; the slaves were freed in autumn 1863 but most had died.
wars.note: Eight ships arrived in December 1862. No territorial change; recorded as the shock that preceded the 1867 epidemic that killed 'the last ariki mau' and the 1888 cession.

wars.name: Wars of the two confederations
wars.outcome: 'From 1724 until 1750, the 'Otu 'Itu fought the Tu'u for control of the island', continuing 'until the 1860s'; no division of the island is recorded.
wars.note: The two hanau existed 'by the 15th century'. Clan names beyond these two are not on the pages opened.

certainty.note: A single island: the coast is the border. What is uncertain is the polity, not its extent: whether the whole island ever had one ariki mau or two confederations.

notes: A state Cliopatria lacks; drawn as a chiefdom (the scope's 'chiefdoms where no state can be shown'). The start year is a bridging choice (confidence 1): the pages offer 300-400, 700-800, 'around 800', 400-1300 and 1200 CE, and no date for Hotu Matuʻa, the ariki mau or the confederations' formation; the reviewer may prefer 800. Not on any page opened: the ariki mau's succession and seat (no capital is recorded), the names of the clans beyond the 'Otu 'Itu and Tu'u, the birdman (tangata manu) cult's date, the matatoa coup, Riro Kainga (not mentioned), the date of the last ariki mau (the 1867 epidemic: 'the dead included the last ariki mau'). Between 1868 and 1876 the French adventurer Dutrou-Bornier ran the island with armed supporters and had Koreto made queen (History of Easter Island page); no territorial event. Alexander Salmon Jr. ran the island from 1878 for about a decade. The 'Council of Rapanui Chiefs' headed by Atamu Tekena is named only in 1888. Region names: the island is a 25 km coordinate circle; the gazetteer has no Easter Island or Hanga Roa entry (gazetteer_names_needed: Easter Island (Rapa Nui) as an admin-1 or region; Isla de Pascua is part of Natural Earth's Valparaíso admin-1).
